## Context / Problem

Discovered from nonblack-brigandish-guillemot: its closing plan review raised this as an advisory finding. ADR 0125 (`docs/adr/0125-opcert-trust-per-environment.md`) replaced repository-pinned op-cert keys with validity-only verification plus an optional per-environment trust list, and the stories under that epic removed the pin file and updated docs and runbooks. User-facing messages in `src` still describe the old model:

- `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py:176`, the re-identify warning (`reidentification_warning`), says `verify.require_environment` "trusts only the own or pinned keys of the environment it names".
- `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py:64` (the `.opcert-key` entry of `CARRY_OVER`, rendered into that same warning) says old-key attestations "fail as `mismatch` unless that key is pinned".

No story's scope or grep check covered `src` prose, so these survived. A sweep of `src` for the same stale model (`git grep -n -i -E 'pinned|out-of-band|own_key|pinned_environment|trusted_environments' -- src`, filtered to op-cert trust prose) found 2 more sites, both developer-facing:

- `src/rebar/attest/opcert.py:6`, the module docstring, says anyone verifies an op-cert "against that environment's out-of-band-pinned public key" (lines 12-15 of the same docstring already note ADR 0125, so the opening sentence contradicts them).
- `src/rebar/_mcp_serving.py:203`, a comment, says it exposes "pinned-key match status" through `/health`; the status comes from `opcert_signing_status` in `src/rebar/_mcp_opcert_health.py:21`, which compares the bound signer against `verify.trusted_opcert_keys`.

Every other `pinned` hit in `src` is about something else (pinned snapshots, pinned policy tables, pinned test wording, authorship keys) and stays.

## Approach

Rewrite the 4 sites to state the ADR 0125 model, matching the verifier's actual behaviour in `src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py` (`verify_opcert_record`, lines 170-310): a certificate verifies on the public key embedded in its signature (trust basis `envelope_key`); when the verifying environment sets `verify.trusted_opcert_keys`, the (environment, key) pair must be listed or the verdict is `untrusted`; `verify.require_environment` turns a certificate naming another environment `foreign_key` and requires a trust list.

- Warning (line ~176): old attestations still certify on the embedded key by default; an environment with `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` trusts them only while its list names the old key; `verify.require_environment` turns a certificate naming another environment `foreign_key`.
- `.opcert-key` carry-over (line ~64): old-key attestations keep verifying on their embedded key, and become `untrusted` only in an environment whose `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` list omits the old key.
- `attest/opcert.py:6`: verified by validity of the embedded key, optionally against the verifier's own trust list.
- `_mcp_serving.py:203`: "Expose the bound signer's trust-list match status through /health".

Prose-only change: no behaviour, config key, env var or flag changes.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py` — the 2 user-facing messages.
- `src/rebar/attest/opcert.py` — module docstring opening sentence.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_serving.py` — the `/health` status comment.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py` — extend `_assert_states_the_current_attestation_policy` to require the ADR 0125 terms and reject the pinned-key wording.

## Testing

`_assert_states_the_current_attestation_policy` (used by `test_reidentification_warning_says_old_attestations_still_certify`) currently checks only `verify.require_environment` and `foreign_key`. Extend it to assert `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` and `untrusted` appear and that `pinned` does not; this fails on the current wording and passes after the fix. Run `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py`, then the full `make verify` before push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both messages describe the ADR 0125 model: validity-only by default, `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` when the verifying environment sets it.
- [ ] `git grep -n -i 'pinned key\|own or pinned\|unless that key is pinned' -- src` prints nothing.
- [ ] `git grep -n -i 'out-of-band-pinned\|pinned-key' -- src` prints nothing.
- [ ] Any test that asserts the old wording is updated in the same change, and `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py` passes with the extended policy assertion (`verify.trusted_opcert_keys` and `untrusted` present, `pinned` absent).
